reading: Four 3x3 red shapes are scattered on a large grid. The output is 7x7: the four shapes laid out 2x2 with a one-cell gap, each keeping its quadrant (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) by relative position.

slots.pieces: the four 3x3 objects (cut by their boxes)
slots.order: each piece's quadrant from its relative position in the input

why: every input object is 3x3; the output is exactly the four boxes placed by relative order with one blank row and column between them
invariants: each shape's pattern and colour are unchanged

reading: A blue structure on top has downward-opening cavities; grey pieces lie below. A grey piece turns red (2) if some rotation/reflection of it, pushed up from below, fills one cavity exactly (extra cells may stick out below the structure).

slots.cavities: background pockets inside the blue rows, closed on left, right and top, open at the bottom
slots.subject: grey (5) objects with an orientation whose cells inside the blue rows equal a cavity exactly and whose other cells lie below the blue rows

why: on every pair the recoloured grey objects are exactly those that can plug a cavity; the rest stay grey

reading: Grey 2x2 blocks stay put. Each single coloured cell moves in a straight line (orthogonal preferred, else diagonal) to the nearest position touching a grey block.
why: every coloured marker ends 8-adjacent to a grey block, reached by the shortest straight move; blocks do not change

reading: Two single cells (top half, bottom half). The output draws a frame: the top half in the top cell's colour (full rows at row 0 and at the cell's row, side columns elsewhere), the bottom half in the bottom cell's colour (full rows at the cell's row and the last row, side columns elsewhere).

slots.colour_top: colour of the marker in the upper half
slots.colour_bottom: colour of the marker in the lower half
slots.lines: full horizontal line through each marker's row, top row and bottom row full, left and right border columns filled

why: every non-background output cell is on the border or a marker row, coloured by the marker in its half

reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block; each of its 8 outer cells shoots a ray of its own colour outward (corners diagonally, edges straight) to the grid border. The centre stays.
why: every ray starts at an outer cell of the block, runs away from the block centre in that cell's direction, and reaches the border

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels cut by separator lines. The top-left panel holds a template shape; in every other panel the template's cells are drawn in the separator colour where the panel is background, keeping cells already there.

slots.template: the shape in the top-left panel
slots.rule: only background cells under the template are painted; existing panel cells stay

why: in every non-template panel, output = input cells plus template positions painted in separator colour
invariants: existing coloured cells in panels unchanged

reading: Background 7 with 3-cell L shapes in grey (5) and red (2). Each red L stamps a copy of itself in colour 3 shifted one cell diagonally through its corner; each grey L stamps a copy in colour 4 shifted one cell diagonally toward its open side. Only background cells are painted; red copies are drawn last.

slots.subject: each L-tromino object
slots.offset: diagonal unit vector from the missing box cell to the corner cell; red: +offset, grey: -offset
slots.paint: background cells only, red copies over grey copies

why: every new cell lies in a one-step diagonal copy of an L in the colour set by that L's colour

reading: A 2x2 block of colour c with some red (2) cells. The block is swept diagonally toward each red corner to the border, leaving a 3-wide diagonal band of colour c; the red cells become c.

slots.subject: the 2x2 block
slots.directions: diagonal from the block centre through each red cell

why: the output is the union of the 2x2 block translated by k steps along each red-corner diagonal, all in the non-red colour

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled by 2: each grey cell becomes the 2x2 block [1 2 / 2 1], each background cell a 2x2 block of 0.
why: every 2x2 output block is the pattern where the input cell is grey and empty otherwise
invariants: layout of grey cells preserved at block scale

reading: Top: three 3x3 colour blocks with one marker cell below each (the legend). Below a full separator row, marker cells are scattered; the output is that lower area with each marker replaced by a 3x3 block centred on it, in the colour the legend gives that marker colour.

slots.legend: marker colour under each top 3x3 block -> that block's colour
slots.field: the panel below the separator row (output size)
slots.subject: single marker cells in the field

why: every 3x3 block in the output sits on a lower-panel marker and has the legend colour of that marker
